identity.title: A Very Compact Extremely High Velocity Flow toward MMS 5/OMC-3 Revealed with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: This study reports a newly found EHV flow and outflow around MMS $5$ in the Orion Molecular Cloud 3 observed with ALMA.

question.value: Do the low-velocity outflow and extremely high-velocity (EHV) jet of the Class 0 protostar MMS 5 follow the nested disk wind or jet entrainment scenario?

evidence.quote: In order to specify the driving mechanism of protostellar outflows, we choose a unique EHV flow associated with MMS 5, which is located in the Orion Molecular Cloud 3 (OMC-3)
This paper uses the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2015.1.00341.S.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Four spectral windows: CO 2-1 and SiO 5-4 with 468.75 MHz bandwidth; C18O and N2D+ with 58.594 MHz; Frequency Division Mode

evidence.quote: Spectral windows allocated for CO $J$=2–1 and SiO $J$=5–4 have a bandwidth of 468.75 MHz
After subtraction of line emissions, the effective bandwidth for the continuum emissions is approximately 1.1 GHz.

arrays.value: ALMA 12-m array (compact and extended) and ACA 7-m array

evidence.quote: Our ALMA 12-m array and ACA 7-m array (Morita-array) observations were performed between 2016 January 29 and September 18
Projected baseline coverage (m) | 7–47 | 10–310 | 10–3130

time_on_source.value: 16 min ACA, 4 min 12-m compact, 8 min 12-m extended

evidence.quote: The total on source time was 16 minutes for the ACA 7-m array, 4 minutes for the ALMA 12-m array compact configuration
with 7 separate executions
Here, $T_{\rm{dust}}$ = 21.5 K is adopted (Sadavoy et al. 2016).

analysis_steps.goal: Fit compact continuum source and derive disk mass

method.value: 2D Gaussian fit with IMFIT; mass from optically thin dust emission formula

evidence.quote: two-dimensional Gaussian fitting tool in CASA (task $\lq\lq$IMFIT") was used.

evidence.quote: We assume a gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100.

validation.value: Residual less than 10% of peak flux

evidence.quote: The residual after extraction of the two-dimensional Gaussian fit is less than 10 % as compared to the peak flux.

method.value: Fit wind-driven shell model z=CR^2 to CO outflow and PV diagrams

evidence.loc: 3.5 Physical Parameters of Outflow and Jet
evidence.quote: The curvature parameter is fit to the outflow shells as $C$ = 0.07 $\rm{arcsec^{-1}}$.

method.value: t_dyn ~ (L_obs/v_obs) tan 50 deg; L_obs measured at 10 sigma contour in channel maps

evidence.loc: 3.5 Physical Parameters of Outflow and Jet
evidence.quote: The projected maximum size of CO $J$=2–1 and SiO $J$=5–4 emission, $L_{\rm obs}$, was measured at the 10 $\sigma$ contour in their channel maps

analysis_steps.goal: Analyze jet knots, precession and launching radius

method.value: Knot spacing, sine fit of wiggle, Keplerian relations for precession and launching radius

evidence.quote: The wiggling is fitted by a simple sine curve in Figure [9](#fig:6-2)(c)
When the protostellar mass of 0.1 $M_\odot$ is assumed[^2], the precession radius becomes approximately 6 AU.

used_for.value: Calibration, CLEAN imaging, IMFIT Gaussian fitting

evidence.quote: Calibration of the raw visibility data was performed by the ALMA observatory with the standard calibration method using the Common Astronomy Software Application (CASA; McMullin et al. 2007).
The total flux, peak flux, and deconvolved size are measured to be $57 \pm 3$ mJy
the mass is estimated to be $M_{1.3\rm{mm}} \sim$ 1.8 $\times\ 10^{-2} M_{\odot}$.

results_numeric.quantity: Outflow inclination to plane of sky

evidence.loc: 3.5 Physical Parameters of Outflow and Jet
evidence.quote: the inclination angle of the outflow axis with respect to the plane of the sky was $i=50^{\circ}$
the period of the cycle can be estimated to be $P \sim 50$ yr
the precession radius becomes approximately 6 AU
The average and median spacings are measured to be $\Delta \theta \simeq$ 0.46 and 0.36 arcsec
our result indicates that the jet appears near the surface of the protostar

findings_qualitative.value: SiO 5-4 traces only the EHV jet, located at the root of the V-shaped CO outflow

evidence.quote: On the other hand, SiO $J$=5–4 emission only traces the EHV flow.

claims.hypothesis: Is the jet younger and shorter than the outflow, as the nested disk wind predicts?
claims.experiment: Measured sizes and dynamical times of CO outflow and CO/SiO jet from channel maps and PV diagrams with inclination 50 deg
claims.result: Jet 11,000 AU vs outflow 14,000 AU; t_dyn ratio ~3
claims.finding: Consistent with nested disk wind, entrainment not fully excluded

evidence.quote: Our results are consistent with the nested wind scenario, although the jet entrainment scenario could not completely be ruled out.

claims.hypothesis: Are the jet and outflow axes aligned?
claims.experiment: Compared position angles of CO outflow and CO/SiO jet

evidence.quote: the difference in P.A between the outflow and the jet is $17^{\circ}$

claims.hypothesis: Does the jet show episodic ejection and precession?
claims.experiment: Identified six knots and fit sine curve to wiggle
claims.result: Ejection every ~9–12 yr, precession ~50 yr at ~6 AU

evidence.quote: The wiggle can be fitted by a sine curve, implying the precession of the jet and the disk.

why_this_data.value: MMS 5 hosts one of the most compact EHV flows, best for studying driving just after protostar formation

evidence.quote: the MMS 5 is the best object to clarify the driving mechanisms of respective velocity flows immediately after protostar formation.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Jet entrainment scenario not completely ruled out

evidence.loc: 4.1 Driving Mechanism of Outflow and Jet
evidence.quote: although the jet entrainment scenario could not completely be ruled out

limitations_admitted.value: Launching points not resolved; further high-resolution observations needed for precession mechanism

evidence.loc: 4.1 Driving Mechanism of Outflow and Jet
evidence.quote: Although we are not able to spatially resolve the outflow and jet launching points (or radii) due to the limited angular resolution

referee_caveats_inferred: Inclination of 50 deg is derived from a simple shell model and strongly affects timescales, with no uncertainty given
Sine fit to six knots with one outlier is weak evidence for precession
Dynamical age ratio is not a unique discriminator between scenarios
